newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL signs Cologne airport freight expansion.
newsitem.headline: DHL signs Cologne airport freight expansion.

text.p: DHL Aviation, part of DHL Worldwide Express has signed a declaration of understanding to open new freight facilities at Cologne/Bonn airport, the airport authority said.
DHL Aviation would take over the freight centre being vacated by TNT Worldwide Express, Flughafen Koeln/Bonn GmbH said.
TNT announced last year it would switch its night-time freighter operations to Liege airport from summer 1998 following local opposition to night flights.
A DHL spokeswoman confirmed the company would step up its Cologne involvement but was unable to say how much would be invested.
DHL had committed itself to using quiet aircraft on a list approved by the German government, the airport said.
The authority put priority on the phasing out of hush-kitted Boeing 727 aircraft being speeded up on noise prevention grounds.
The new DHL freight centre would grow to 20,000 square metres of operational space and additional office space by 2000, the airport said.

The DHL Cologne freight tonnage of 17,000 tonnes a year would grow in coming years but would stay at about 18 daily movements due to the use of larger aircraft, it added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax: 5017
